full_judgment:
8. It is at this juncture that the lower appellate Court is found to embark upon a detailed analysis of the facts and evidence before it and of the relevant law attracted to this case. The starting point for the lower appellate Court has been that of the presumption that attaches upon the act of registration, to the effect that registration proceedings are to be deemed to have been regularly and honestly carried out unless it is otherwise proven by the party who attempts to establish facts to the contrary. This Court finds that the lower appellate Court proceeded on the right track in this regard and also notes that the fact that such a presumption may appropriately be made in such cases has been duly endorsed in the case of Gangamoyi Debi vs Troiluckhya Nath Chowdhury reported in 33 Indian Appeals, 60. In Gangamoyi Devi s case it was observed thus at page 65: 

 আইনতঃ রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত দলিলের রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত কার্যক্রম সঠিক বলিয়াই বিবেচনা করিতে হইবে। ইহার বিপরীতে প্রমাণের দায়িত্ব যিনি ইহা বলিবেন যে, যথাযথভাবে রেজিষ্ট্রি হয় নাই। তৎমর্মে ২৬ ডিিএল, আর, এ নরেন্দ্র নাথ বনাম আঃ রহমান মামলায় ৪৫ পৃষ্ঠায় আইনের এই সিদ্ধান্ত দিয়াছেন যে, Presumption that the document was duly registered Burden of proof when a party says the contrary. অপর একটি সিদ্ধান্তে মহামান্য সুপ্রীমকোর্ট ৩৯ ডিএলআর (এডি) এর ২২৩ পৃষ্ঠায় আইনের এই সিদ্ধান্ত দিয়াছেন যে, Presumption of law that the registration proceedings were regular and honestly carried out. 

 In this regard, that Court further noted pertinently  that from the plaint it is evident that though the plaintiff has raised questions about the fact of execution of the deed she has not raised any specific objection as to the fact of process of registration. This led the lower appellate Court to conclude that so far as registration is concerned the legal presumption of sufficiency. of that process has not been rebutted sufficiently by the plaintiff in this case. Relying upon the finding in A Rahman vs A Rahim Gazi reported in 35 DLR 132, that the plaintiff " 

 "Thus, a hiba in such circumstances should be taken to be perfectly valid even without an express delivery of possession of the subjectmatter of the gift. By that reason, it is this Court's view that the academic exercise undertaken by the lower appellate Court with regard to finding an intention to give, and the taking of constructive possession by the donee of the suit land is well founded in law. In this regard, this Court finds no reason to accept the 'submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the presumption as relied upon by the lower appellate Court in the impugned judgment, although substantiated by that Court by reference to judicial precedents, must somehow be considered negated by reason of debilitating facts as otherwise asserted by the petitioner. In further substantiation of its finding in this regard the lower appellate Court also found reason to question the plaintiff's stand taken in this case against the hiba deed without also challenging a waqf deed executed by her husband Anfar Uddin on the same date under allegedly same circumstances. It is also wondered why other transactions entered into by her husband in transferring his other properties on subsequent dates were never questioned by the plaintiff. Moreover, the said Anfar Uddin, the executor of the disputed deed, who lived for a period of four years thereafter never himself took any initiative to question or challenge the circumstances under which the gift deed is alleged to have been executed and registered. This Court is satisfied that all these issues, facts and the application of relevant law cumulatively operated in the mind of the learned Additional District Judge to correctly find for a proper execution and registration of the deed in question thereby necessitating a reversal of the trial Court's judgment and decree. This Court is further satisfied that the lower appellate Court allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree of the Trial Court on a proper consideration of facts and evidence and an almost exhaustive enunciation of the law. That being the case, this Court finds no reason to interfere with that appellate decision and judgment sitting in revisional jurisdiction.
